 Expectations be damned: Sounders enter playoffs with something to prove
 Coming off arguably their most disappointing regular season ever, the Sounders have one chance to salvage their campaign.
 By 
 Jeremiah Oshan

 SEATTLE – Basically ever since they entered MLS, a successful Seattle Sounders season has been effectively measured by their trophy count. Absent actual silverware, how they performed in the MLS playoffs is often used as a proxy.
 They’ve been remarkably successful on both counts.
 In eight of their previous 17 seasons, the Sounders have claimed at least one major trophy. In the other nine, they’ve twice made it to MLS Cup, gotten to the Western Conference finals two more times, and only once failed to get at least as far as the conference semifinals. They’ve generally been considered at least dark-horse contenders to win MLS Cup every year they’ve made the playoffs.
 Expectations as they head into this year’s playoffs are something short of that. 
 Not only are the Sounders the West’s No. 8 seed, they also finished tied for the 14th most points in MLS and were 16th in the Supporters’ Shield race, marking just the second time they’ve ever finished in the lower half of the league’s overall standings. For the first time, the Sounders posted a negative goal-difference (-2), and their 12 wins were tied for the fewest they’ve had in a 34-game season.
 The Sounders insist that they aren’t letting any of that impact their internal expectations for the Western Conference Wild Card game against Real Salt Lake on Thursday.
 "I don’t think it changes anything," Sounders midfielder Paul Rothrock said. "Every year, this club expects trophies, and we haven’t won a trophy yet. That's the expectation." While outsiders may not be giving the Sounders much of a chance to make a serious run at a third MLS Cup, the mood inside the locker room is that this is still the same team that started the season with aspirations of winning every competition it entered. 
 It’s also a roster whose core guided the Sounders to four MLS Cup finals in five years, made history by winning Concacaf and delivered a Leagues Cup trophy last year. 
 "We started the season in a great way, that's the team we feel like we are," Sounders captain Cristian Roldan said. "Our season took a spiral, and we need to get back into who we think we are. I think we think very highly of ourselves in the locker room. I think we think that we’re a good team, but we've got to show it come Thursday."
 The Sounders won just five games after starting the season 7–1–3, which famously included an eight-game losing streak and a 13-game winless run, both club records. Even after righting the ship with a four-game winning streak, the Sounders closed out the season with 1–3–2 record over their final six.
 This is their last chance to show who they really are.
 "I think there’s a little bit of a chip on their shoulders," Sounders head coach Brian Schmetzer said. "I think they’re, in some ways, trying to learn from some of the adversity they went through, and that's a healthy human trait, to try and reflect, learn and be better. I was happy with what some of the guys have been saying."
 While playoff seeding matters – no Wild Card team has advanced beyond the conference semifinals – there is an underlying truth to the belief that playoffs are effectively a new season. Unlikely as it may be to occur, a hot run would wash away a lot of the frustrations over the past six months. 
 "At the end of December, the team that wins the trophy is the one that beats everyone anyway," Sounders goalkeeper Andrew Thomas said. "It doesn't matter if you’re in first or last. This season has maybe not reflected the ability that I think is in this group. Now we have the opportunity to fix some of that. The opportunity is the same for us as it is for anyone else. I’m excited for it."
 Jeremiah Oshan 
 I’ve been working in journalism for three decades and covering the Sounders since 2010. I take pride in trying to understand what fans most want to know and helping them understand the game.
